top_choice_rationale: Zurita (P003) remains my first choice on public knowledge of the work, which I have not freshly read or independently verified. The citation is limited to the printed poems, from Purgatory and Anteparadise onward, with the landscape interventions treated as context. On that basis I find in him the most distinctive voice and the most radical formal conception on the shortlist: mourning, the damaged body and the national landscape recur in a liturgical diction over about five decades. His project also seems to me less indebted to an established tradition than the encyclopedic visionary novel. Poetry in translation is the hardest ground, and my knowledge of the later books is thinner than of the early sequences. Colleagues' doubts that the poems alone carry the case are real and I cannot fully dispel them. I therefore rank Cărtărescu (P001) second, as the best-evidenced whole-oeuvre alternative, with the open question of whether his late books extend the project or only enlarge it. Can Xue (P002) is third. I cannot show development in her method, but I treat that as a limit on my confidence and not as a verdict, and translation risk applies equally to all candidates. Michon (P004) is fourth. His sentence-level achievement is outstanding, but a slender and narrow oeuvre fits the whole-body standard less well. No award (P000) is last, because several credible literary cases are available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to any shortlisted writer is recorded. My scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan is context only, though it may incline me toward poetry. I disclose that and do not treat it as evidence of merit.
